blocks.text: el-buṭm). The press residues are called in Jewish [=Jewish] Aramaic [=Aramaic] כוספא דבטמי (Hg. [=Halachot gedolot, ed. Hildesheimer] 58_{5. 29}).

Guigues [=P. Guigues, Le livre de l'art du Traitement] p. [=page] 39 says: The green grains, granum viride (الحبّة الخضراء [al-ḥabba al-khaḍrāʾ]) of the Middle Ages, are the fruits of the terebinth, P. Tereb. L. [=Linnaeus]. They have been confused with pistachios, fusṭuḳ, fruits of P. vera L. Moreover, the green grains are still used as food today. It is above all in Mesopotamia that the fruits of the terebinth, buṭm, are edible.

בטנה, bŏṭnā,*) [assyr. [=Assyrian] buṭnu, Zimmern AF. [=H. Zimmern, Akkadische Fremdwörter] 54; palmyr. [=Palmyrene] בר בוטן**) n. pr. [=nomen proprium] Chajes, Onomatolog. [=H. P. Chajes, Beiträge zur nordsemitischen Onomatologie] 12] also Mishnaic. Švi [=Mishnah tractate Shevi'it] 7, 5: בוטנא, LA. [=variant reading] בטנה (TŠvi [=Tosefta Shevi'it, ed. Zuckermandel] 5, 68_{14}, Schwarz [=A. Schwarz's Tosefta editions and commentary] p. 215), once also Targ. [=Targum] בוטנין Gn. [=Genesis] 43, 11.

boṭnā is a native tree, whereas pistachios are imported from abroad (j Dem. [=Jerusalem Talmud, tractate Demai, ed. Krotoschin] 2, 22^{b}_{69}). These come to Eretz Yisrael from northern Syria (Rosen [=?], Pf. [=Löw, Aramäische Pflanzennamen] 69).

The cited Mishnah and T. [=Tosefta, ed. Zuckermandel] passage speaks of young, edible shoots, לולב. The following are named: a) זרדים, b) הרובים, c) אלה, d) בוטנה, e) אטדין, f) אדיל. c) according to Maimūnī [=Maimonides, commentary on the Mishnah] correctly ballūṭ,***) d. h. [=that is] ʾallā oak, not ʾēlā! Gal. [=Galen, Opera omnia, ed. Kühn] 6, 644 βλαστοὶ τερμίνθου [blastoi terminthou]! e) ῥάμνου [rhamnou]. He says: the terebinth shoots are pickled in vinegar or brine (Sachau, Inedita [=Eduard Sachau, Inedita Syriaca] 95).

The place name bŏṭnā alone proves that the foreign pistachio cannot be meant. As a place name Arabic buṭm occurs: Socin, Ortsapell. [=Albert Socin, Arabic place appellatives] ZDPV. [=Zeitschrift des Deutschen Palästina-Vereins] 22, 18: challet il-buṭm terebinth valley 31, 199, maḳāṭiʿ el-buṭmi terebinth quarry (31, 183).

בטנה Jos. [=Joshua] 13, 26 according to Robinson [=Edward Robinson, Palästina] 3, 924 baṭne south of eṣ-ṣalt (Schwarz, Tebuot haareṣ [=Joseph Schwarz, Tevuot ha-Aretz] ed. Luncz, p. 271 n [=note]). A place boṭnā also jAz. [=Jerusalem Talmud, tractate Avodah Zarah] 1, 39^{d}_{27} = בטנן B. r. [=Bereshit Rabba, ed. Theodor and Albeck] 47 end. The fair at the terebinth ירידה של בוטנה (ZAW. [=Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft] 29, 217. 221). S. Klein [=Samuel Klein, professor in Jerusalem] has combined this with the market of בית האילם MT. 185_{17} Hoffm. [=Midrash Tannaim, ed. D. Hoffmann], בית אילנים Sifre 2, 306, 132_{6} Friedm. [=Sifre, ed. M. Friedmann].

With the place name bŏtnā Dérenbourg [=Joseph Derenbourg, Essai sur l'histoire et la géographie de la Palestine] has associated בטנית bŏṭnīt, a female proselyte from boṭnā (Sabb. [=tractate Shabbat] 24, 5. Beza 3, 8. T. 3, 205_{27}. TMen [=Tosefta Menahot] 13, 533_{33}. [Pes. [=tractate Pesahim] 57^{a}] Ned. [=tractate Nedarim] 23^{a}. M. Zizit [=Massekhet Zizit] p. 23_{6} Kirchheim [=Raphael Kirchheim, Septem libri Talmudici parvi Hierosolymitani] = Semaḥ. [=tractate Semahot] 12 [p. 98_{12} Romm. [=Romm edition (Vilna) of the Talmud] קטנים read, with M. Zizit, Šibbŏlē [=Shibbole ha-Leket, ed. S. Buber] 341 Buber [=Salomon Buber] and R. [=Rabbi] Elia Wilna, בטנית. ZAW. 29, 216).
On 1 K. [=1 Kings] 7, 20 מלעמת הבטן, F. Perles neue Anal. [=Felix Perles, Analekten zur Textkritik des Alten Testaments, Neue Folge] 75 recalls boṭnīm.
S. Klein (I. 1926) refers to MS. [=Monatsschrift für Geschichte und Wissenschaft des Judentums] 1910, 22 בית אילונים for [בית] בטנה and combines with it the name Abba Saul boṭnīt.
Flora [=Immanuel Löw, Die Flora der Juden] 3, 254 is to be corrected accordingly.
